t: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE.
f: The Hijrah took place in 610 CE.
x: The Hijrah was in 622 CE. Revelation began around 610 CE.

t: The Battle of Badr was the first major battle of Islam.
f: The Battle of Uhud was the first major battle of Islam.
x: Badr (2 AH) came first, Uhud (3 AH) a year later.

t: The Muslims at Badr numbered a little over three hundred.
f: The Muslims at Badr numbered about three thousand.
x: Al-Bara' said the people of Badr were about the number of Talut's men, a little over three hundred.

t: The archers' leaving their post turned the tide at Uhud.
f: The archers' leaving their post turned the tide at Badr.
x: At Uhud the archers left the hill against orders, and the Muslims were attacked from behind.

t: A trench was dug around Madinah in the Battle of the Confederates.
f: A trench was dug around Makkah in the Battle of Hunayn.
x: The trench (khandaq) protected Madinah against the Confederates.

t: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was made with Quraysh.
f: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was made with the Byzantines.
x: Hudaybiyyah was a truce with Quraysh in 6 AH.

t: Surah Al-Fath was revealed after Hudaybiyyah.
f: Surah Al-Fath was revealed after the Battle of Badr.
x: Surah Al-Fath came on the return from Hudaybiyyah, calling the treaty a clear victory.

t: The Battle of Hunayn is named in the Qur'an.
f: The Battle of Uhud is named in the Qur'an.
x: Surah At-Tawbah names Hunayn. Uhud is described but not named.

t: The Expedition of Tabuk was against the Byzantines.
f: The Expedition of Tabuk was against the Persians.
x: Tabuk, in 9 AH, was a march north to face the Byzantines.

t: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH.
f: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 6 AH.
x: The Prophet's only Hajj was in 10 AH, months before his death.

t: "Today I have perfected your religion" was revealed at Arafah.
f: "Today I have perfected your religion" was revealed at Badr.
x: Umar said this verse was revealed on a Friday, while the Prophet ﷺ stood at Arafah.

t: The qiblah was changed in the second year after the Hijrah.
f: The qiblah was changed in the tenth year after the Hijrah.
x: The qiblah changed about sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah.

t: The Muslims first faced Jerusalem in prayer.
f: The Muslims first faced Ta'if in prayer.
x: They prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis before facing the Ka'bah.

t: The first migration was to Abyssinia.
f: The first migration was to Yemen.
x: Persecuted Muslims first migrated to Abyssinia, ruled by the Negus.

t: The Year of Sorrow saw the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah.
f: The Year of Sorrow saw the deaths of Abu Bakr and Umar.
x: Abu Talib and Khadijah died in the same year, before the Hijrah.

t: The Prophet ﷺ travelled to Ta'if to invite its people.
f: The Prophet ﷺ travelled to Damascus to invite its people.
x: He went to Ta'if, and its people rejected him.

t: The Ansar were the Muslims of Madinah.
f: The Ansar were the Muslims who migrated from Makkah.
x: The Ansar (helpers) were the people of Madinah. The migrants were the Muhajirun.

t: The Muhajirun were the Muslims who migrated from Makkah.
f: The Muhajirun were the original people of Madinah.
x: The Muhajirun migrated. The Ansar received them.

t: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
f: Umar accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
x: Abu Bakr was his companion in the cave.

t: Ali slept in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijrah.
f: Uthman slept in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijrah.
x: Ali stayed behind in his bed and later returned the trusts people had left with the Prophet ﷺ.

t: Zayd ibn Harithah is the only companion named in the Qur'an.
f: Abu Bakr is the only companion named in the Qur'an.
x: Zayd is named in Surah Al-Ahzab.

t: Abu Lahab is the only opponent of the Prophet named in the Qur'an.
f: Abu Jahl is named in the Qur'an.
x: Surah Al-Masad names Abu Lahab. Abu Jahl is not named.

t: Hamzah was martyred at Uhud.
f: Hamzah was martyred at Badr.
x: Hamzah fought at Badr and was martyred at Uhud.

t: Khalid ibn al-Walid was called the Sword of Allah.
f: Abu Bakr was called the Sword of Allah.
x: The Prophet ﷺ called Khalid a sword from the swords of Allah.

t: Abu Ubaydah was called the trustworthy one of this ummah.
f: Khalid was called the trustworthy one of this ummah.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the trustworthy one of this ummah is Abu Ubaydah.

t: Uthman married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ.
f: Ali married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ.
x: Uthman married Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum. Ali married Fatimah.

t: Abu Hurayrah narrated more hadith than any other companion.
f: Abu Bakr narrated more hadith than any other companion.
x: Abu Hurayrah narrated the most hadith of all.

t: Anas ibn Malik served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years.
f: Anas ibn Malik served the Prophet ﷺ for two years.
x: Anas said he served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years.

t: Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Yemen.
f: Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Persia.
x: The Prophet ﷺ sent Mu'adh to Yemen.

t: The Qur'an was first gathered into one volume under Abu Bakr.
f: The Qur'an was first gathered into one volume under Ali.
x: After Yamamah, Zayd ibn Thabit gathered it under Abu Bakr.

t: Zayd ibn Thabit led the gathering of the Qur'an.
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the gathering of the Qur'an.
x: Abu Bakr gave the task to Zayd ibn Thabit, a scribe of revelation.

t: Uthman sent standard copies of the Qur'an to the main cities.
f: Mu'awiyah sent standard copies of the Qur'an to the main cities.
x: Uthman had copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent them out.

t: Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah of the prayer.
f: Al-Fatihah is recited only in the first rak'ah of the prayer.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer for one who does not recite Al-Fatihah.

t: There are fifteen places of prostration in the Qur'an in the common count.
f: There are fifty places of prostration in the Qur'an in the common count.
x: The mushaf marks fifteen verses of prostration.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses, Al-Mulk, intercedes for the one who recites it.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said Surah Al-Kawthar intercedes for the one who recites it until he is forgiven.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses interceded for a man until he was forgiven: Tabarak alladhi biyadihil-mulk.

t: Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Qur'an.
f: Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to half of the Qur'an.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said Al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Qur'an.

t: Surah Al-Kahf is recommended on Fridays.
f: Surah Al-Kahf is recommended on Mondays.
x: Reciting Al-Kahf on Friday is narrated to bring light between the two Fridays.

t: Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest verse in the Qur'an.
f: The last verse of Al-Baqarah is the greatest verse in the Qur'an.
x: The Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy that Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest verse.

t: The last two verses of Al-Baqarah suffice the one who recites them at night.
f: The last two verses of Al-Fatihah suffice the one who recites them at night.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever recites the last two verses of Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.

t: Shaytan flees from a house where Al-Baqarah is recited.
f: Shaytan flees from a house where poetry is recited.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan flees from the house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited.

t: Isa will return before the end of time.
f: Musa will return before the end of time.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the son of Maryam will descend as a just ruler.

t: The Dajjal is blind in one eye.
f: The Dajjal has three eyes.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the Dajjal is blind in one eye.

t: Ya'juj and Ma'juj were held back by a barrier.
f: Ya'juj and Ma'juj were held back by a river.
x: Dhul-Qarnayn built a barrier against them.

t: Dhul-Qarnayn built a wall of iron and copper.
f: Dhul-Qarnayn built a wall of gold and silver.
x: He asked for iron blocks and poured molten copper over them.

t: Musa met al-Khidr where the two seas meet.
f: Musa met al-Khidr in Egypt's palace.
x: Musa travelled to the junction of the two seas to meet the servant of Allah.

t: Al-Khidr damaged a boat to save it from a king.
f: Al-Khidr built a boat to escape a flood.
x: He made a hole in the boat because a king was seizing every good boat.

t: The People of the Cave slept for 309 years.
f: The People of the Cave slept for 40 years.
x: They stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine.

t: Luqman advised his son not to associate partners with Allah.
f: Luqman advised his son to seek kingship.
x: Luqman told his son, "Do not ascribe partners to Allah."

t: Sulayman had jinn working for him.
f: Nuh had jinn working for him.
x: Jinn worked for Sulayman by his Lord's leave.

t: Dawud killed Jalut.
f: Talut killed Jalut.
x: Allah says Dawud killed Jalut.

t: Ayyub is known for his patience in illness.
f: Ayyub is known for building the Ka'bah.
x: Allah says of Ayyub, "We found him patient."

t: Yunus is called Dhun-Nun in the Qur'an.
f: Yusuf is called Dhun-Nun in the Qur'an.
x: Dhun-Nun, the man of the fish, is Yunus.

t: Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan.
f: Shu'ayb was sent to 'Ad.
x: Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan. Hud was sent to 'Ad.

t: Hud was sent to the people of 'Ad.
f: Hud was sent to the people of Thamud.
x: Hud was sent to 'Ad. Salih was sent to Thamud.

t: Salih was sent to Thamud.
f: Salih was sent to Madyan.
x: Salih was sent to Thamud.

t: Lut's people lived in the time of Ibrahim.
f: Lut's people lived in the time of Isa.
x: Lut believed in Ibrahim and migrated with him.

t: Zakariyya was the guardian of Maryam.
f: Imran was the guardian of Maryam in the sanctuary.
x: Allah placed Maryam in the care of Zakariyya.

t: Yahya was the son of Zakariyya.
f: Yahya was the son of Imran.
x: Yahya was born to Zakariyya in his old age.

t: Isma'il helped his father build the Ka'bah.
f: Ishaq helped his father build the Ka'bah.
x: Ibrahim and Isma'il raised the foundations of the House.

t: Ibrahim's father was named Azar in the Qur'an.
f: Ibrahim's father was named Imran in the Qur'an.
x: Surah Al-An'am names Ibrahim's father Azar.

t: Qarun was swallowed by the earth.
f: Qarun drowned in the sea.
x: Allah caused the earth to swallow Qarun. Fir'awn drowned.

t: Haman was the minister of Fir'awn.
f: Haman was the brother of Musa.
x: Haman served Fir'awn. Musa's brother was Harun.

t: Surah Al-Qadr says the angels and the Spirit descend on Laylat al-Qadr.
f: Surah Al-Qadr says the jinn descend on Laylat al-Qadr.
x: Surah Al-Qadr: the angels and the Spirit descend in it by the permission of their Lord.

t: I'tikaf is usually done in the last ten days of Ramadan.
f: I'tikaf is only allowed in the first ten days of Ramadan.
x: The Prophet ﷺ used to make i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan.

t: Zakat has eight categories of recipients.
f: Zakat has three categories of recipients.
x: Surah At-Tawbah lists eight categories.

t: Travellers may shorten four-rak'ah prayers to two.
f: Travellers may shorten Maghrib to one rak'ah.
x: Four-rak'ah prayers are shortened. Maghrib and Fajr are not.

t: Witr is prayed after Isha.
f: Witr is prayed before Fajr's adhan only on Fridays.
x: Witr is prayed between Isha and Fajr.

t: Tahajjud is prayed at night.
f: Tahajjud is prayed at noon.
x: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ, "And in some part of the night, pray tahajjud."

t: The best prayer after the obligatory ones is the night prayer.
f: The best prayer after the obligatory ones is the Duha prayer.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the best prayer after the obligatory ones is the prayer at night.

t: Fasting the day of Arafah expiates two years of sins.
f: Fasting the day of Arafah expiates ten years of sins.
x: It expiates the year before and the year after.

t: Fasting Ashura expiates the previous year.
f: Fasting Ashura expiates the next ten years.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said it expiates the year before.

t: The miqat for the people of Madinah is Dhul-Hulayfah.
f: The miqat for the people of Madinah is Yalamlam.
x: Dhul-Hulayfah is Madinah's miqat. Yalamlam is Yemen's.

t: Pilgrims spend the night at Muzdalifah after Arafah.
f: Pilgrims spend the night at Ta'if after Arafah.
x: After sunset at Arafah they go to Muzdalifah.

t: Hajar ran between Safa and Marwah seven times.
f: Hajar ran between Arafah and Mina seven times.
x: Hajar ran between Safa and Marwah looking for water, and pilgrims do the same.

t: Zamzam appeared for Hajar and her son.
f: Zamzam was dug by Musa.
x: Zamzam gushed forth for Hajar and Isma'il.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who own the most land.
x: He said, "The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it."

t: The Prophet ﷺ said none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said none of you truly believes until he owns gold.
x: Love for your brother what you love for yourself.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or stay silent.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever believes in Allah should speak as much as possible.
x: Speak good or remain silent.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said the upper hand is better than the lower hand.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said the lower hand is better than the upper hand.
x: The giving hand is better than the receiving hand.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said Paradise is surrounded by hardships.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said the Fire is surrounded by hardships.
x: Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire by desires.

t: The Prophet ﷺ forbade cutting ties of kinship.
f: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged cutting ties with relatives.
x: He said the one who cuts ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.

t: Backbiting is compared in the Qur'an to eating a dead brother's flesh.
f: Backbiting is compared in the Qur'an to drinking wine.
x: Surah Al-Hujurat makes this comparison.

t: Surah Al-Hujurat teaches not to mock other people.
f: Surah Al-Hujurat teaches that mocking is allowed.
x: It says, "Let not a people mock another people."

t: Allah says the most honoured of you is the most righteous.
f: Allah says the most honoured of you is the richest.
x: Surah Al-Hujurat: the noblest of you with Allah is the most pious.

t: The Qur'an forbids wine and gambling.
f: The Qur'an forbids honey and milk.
x: Surah Al-Ma'idah calls wine and gambling an abomination of Satan's work.

t: Pork is forbidden in the Qur'an.
f: Fish is forbidden in the Qur'an.
x: The Qur'an forbids carrion, blood and the flesh of swine. Seafood is lawful.

t: Interest (riba) is forbidden in the Qur'an.
f: Trade is forbidden in the Qur'an.
x: Allah permitted trade and forbade usury.

t: Allah says there is no compulsion in religion.
f: Allah says people must be forced into religion.
x: Al-Baqarah 256: there is no compulsion in religion.

t: The Qur'an calls the believers brothers.
f: The Qur'an calls the believers strangers to one another.
x: Surah Al-Hujurat: the believers are nothing but brothers.

t: Kindness to parents comes right after worshipping Allah in Surah Al-Isra.
f: Surah Al-Isra allows saying "uff" to parents.
x: Al-Isra commands goodness to parents and forbids even saying "uff".

t: Surah Al-Asr says mankind is in loss except those who believe and do good.
f: Surah Al-Asr says mankind is always successful.
x: Al-Asr: man is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds and counsel truth and patience.

t: Surah Al-Ma'un warns those who pray only to be seen.
f: Surah Al-Ma'un praises those who pray only to be seen.
x: It warns "those who want to be seen".

t: Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah that He is near and answers the caller.
f: Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah that He is far and does not answer.
x: When My servants ask you about Me, I am near.

t: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
f: Allah burdens every soul beyond what it can bear.
x: The end of Al-Baqarah says Allah tasks no soul beyond its capacity.

t: Allah says with hardship comes ease.
f: Allah says with ease comes only hardship.
x: Surah Ash-Sharh: with hardship comes ease, twice.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said the strongest believer is more beloved to Allah than the weak one, and in both there is good.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said there is no good in a weak believer.
x: He said the strong believer is better and more beloved, and in each there is good.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the biggest, even if rare.
x: The most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular, even if little.

t: Sujud is the position in which a servant is closest to his Lord.
f: Ruku' is the position in which a servant is closest to his Lord.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating.

t: The angels Munkar and Nakir question the dead in the grave.
f: The angels Harut and Marut question the dead in the grave.
x: A hadith in al-Tirmidhi names Munkar and Nakir.

t: Malik is the keeper of Hell.
f: Ridwan is named in the Qur'an as the keeper of Hell.
x: The Qur'an names Malik as the keeper of the Fire.

t: Harut and Marut were sent down in Babylon.
f: Harut and Marut were sent down in Makkah.
x: Al-Baqarah places them in Babylon.

t: Every child is born on the fitrah.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said every child is born without any nature.
x: Every child is born upon the natural disposition.

t: The Prophet ﷺ said the world is a prison for the believer.
f: The Prophet ﷺ said the world is a paradise for the believer.
x: The world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's paradise.

t: The Prophet ﷺ prayed at night until his feet swelled.
f: The Prophet ﷺ never prayed at night.
x: He prayed until his feet swelled, and said, "Should I not be a grateful servant?"
